results.title: Review of n8n by jess - Product Hunt
results.content: Workflow automation for technical people What do you think about n8n? What do people think of n8n? The community submitted 124 reviews to tell us what they like about n8n, what n8n can do better, and You start out with Zapier, then graduate to Make.com, before ending up at n8n. n8n is the greatest prototyping, building, and automation tool to date. It's been awesome watching the team grow n8n over the past 2 years. I've been using n8n for automation at our HCD firm since many of our clients are government and healthcare, and we can self host n8n, keeping our data secure and private. One of the best parts of n8n, that makes it so usable is their community forum. We're excited to continue the journey with n8n! I've been using n8n for two years in self host inside my Growth company, and I have to say, I could not live without it now. Best workflow automation tool in the market. @janoberhauser & the team, thanks for making my life easier. I've been using n8n for almost 4 years now. Zapier and Make are an absolute hell to use vs. Once you get used to it, you will have a hard time going back to Zapier or Make. The simplicity and power of being able to draw your workflow on a canvas is great when compared to the linear approach of Zapier (Come on, paths are half-baked, tedious, and limited to 5) or the surprisingly rigid approach of Make (Why do I need a router & filter to split things?) The support for Javascript in any node with expressions also increases the functionality so much. i wish there's the same for Jivochat ♥ GLWS Amazed to see how much n8n progressed in these years, and to be part of this story makes me very happy. I work for n8n for nearly 3 years now. I think the biggest winners are the people that n8n empowered to do amazing things, regardless of coding skill. I have been using N8N about a month. Its visual flow editing makes it much easier for others to 'read' than alternative automation products.

Hi Makers, Builders, and Founders, My background is in finance, and I saw first-hand how fast automation costs from platforms like Zapier or Make can crush a scale-up. Worse, relying solely on their cloud means **you don't own your data or your workflows.**. I solved this for my agency, Azenflow, and now for our clients, by going **100% Open Source** with the powerful platform, **n8n**. --- **🤯 The Problem I Solved (And You Should Too)**. 1. **Cost:** Automation bills were projected to hit $800/month by year-end. With n8n, this is $0 in license fees. 2. **Compliance:** For all EU-based companies, **Data Sovereignty is non-negotiable**. We achieve this by self-hosting our n8n stack (RGPD compliance). **🛠️ The 3-Step Open-Source Architecture** This is the architecture we deploy to achieve Zapier-killing power:. 1. **The Engine (n8n):** Powerful open-source workflow automation. Requires more setup, but allows custom JS and complex logic. 2. **The Host (Your Cloud):** We deploy it in a dedicated, controlled environment for guaranteed **data sovereignty**. 3. **The Brain (AI Integration):** n8n easily integrates LLMs/AI via API, putting you in control of the cost and keys. --- **❓ Open Challenge to the Community** **Has anyone else made the leap from proprietary automation to Open Source (n8n, self-hosted solutions, etc.)?**. What were your biggest pain points? *I’m an expert n8n Architect, happy to answer* ***any*** *technical or business questions about making this migration. Title: FlowPulse — Workflow observability for n8n, Make, Zapier & more
# Know when your automations run, fail, or go quiet. FlowPulse is the run ledger for n8n, Make, Zapier, and custom stacks—one API for success and failure, a single place to see history, reports, and alerts. When an automation stops running, most platforms won’t shout about it. Execution history is scattered across n8n, Make, Zapier, and cron—no single SLA across tools. Run-level truth is enough to act: did it execute, did it succeed, how long did it take—plus IDs to jump back to the source system. ### Define workflows in FlowPulse. FlowPulse tracks them by stable IDs—rename tools on your side without breaking reporting. ### Send success and failure at the boundary. Call the ingest API from the end of your success path and your failure path. Use your ingestion key—same pattern for n8n HTTP modules, Make webhooks, Zapier, or code. `POST /api/v1/ingest/run-success. ### Watch runs, reports, and alerts. See run history, failure trends, and success rates. Add alert rules for failures, thresholds, durations, and no-run detection—delivered to your destinations. FlowPulse is optimized for fast instrumentation: one execution is one run, with the context you need to debug in your automation tool. ### Success and failure. ### Stable workflow IDs. Events reference FlowPulse workflow IDs so renames do not fragment history. ### Runs and history. Failure rates, error breakdowns, and trends over time—per workflow and source. Thresholds, rates, durations, and no-run detection—wired to your destinations. The same information architecture wherever you work: dashboard overview, workflows, runs, reports, and alerts. At-a-glance health: workflows, run volume, failures, and recent activity across the last 24 hours. ### Workflows. Organize every automation you monitor; open a workflow for detail and recent runs. ## Workflows. Rules for run status, rates, durations, and silence—delivered to the destinations you configure. Start free today—no credit card required. No credit card required to start. No. You add HTTP calls at the end of your success and failure paths—or the closest equivalent in your platform. A failed run is an execution that reported failure. Ingestion uses API keys scoped to your workspace. At minimum: your FlowPulse workflow identifier. Create a workspace, add your first workflow, and send your first event in minutes.
